ei.title: Practice 01 — 윤리적 기준이 소비자들의 소비성향에 미치는 영향
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers ①<u>conducted</u> a series of experiments. They ②<u>showing</u> consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but ③<u>told</u> one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were ④<u>willing</u> to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① conducted=실시했다(과거동사 정상), ② showed→showing 오류(주어 They에 이어지는 본동사이므로 과거형 필요), ③ told=말했다(과거동사 정상), ④ willing=기꺼이~하는(형용사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① conducted: 'researchers conducted a series of experiments' — 과거 동사 정상
✅ ② showing: 'They showed consumers the same products'에서 showed는 주어 They에 연결된 본동사여야 함. showing(현재분사)으로 바꾸면 문장에 주동사가 없어져 구조 오류 ← 정답
❌ ③ told: 'but told one group the items had been made' — 과거 동사 정상
❌ ④ willing: 'consumers were willing to pay' — be willing to 구문 정상
det.tip: 주어(They)에 연결된 본동사는 과거형(showed)이어야 함. showing은 분사로 주동사 역할 불가

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① relatively=상대적으로(부사 정상), ② using=사용하여(분사구문 정상), ③ were willing→was willing 오류(복수주어 consumers에 단수동사 불가), ④ ethically=윤리적으로(부사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① relatively: 'relatively homogeneous' — 부사로 형용사 수식, 정상
❌ ② using: 'had been made using high ethical standards' — 분사구문으로 정상
✅ ③ was willing: 'consumers were willing to pay' — 주어 consumers는 복수이므로 were가 맞음. was로 바꾸면 수 일치 오류 ← 정답
❌ ④ ethically: 'ethically made goods' — 부사로 과거분사 수식 정상
det.tip: 주어 consumers(복수) → 동사 were(복수). was는 단수 주어에 사용

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ to find out=알아내기 위해(to부정사 정상), ② had been made→has been made 오류(시제 일치 위반), ① ethically=윤리적으로(부사 정상), ④ shaping=형성하는 데(동명사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ② ethically: 'ethically made goods' — 부사로 과거분사 수식 정상
✅ ① has been made: 'told one group the items had been made' — 과거시제 told에 종속된 간접화법 절은 시제 일치로 had been made(과거완료)여야 함. has been made(현재완료)로 바꾸면 시제 불일치 ← 정답
❌ ③ to find out: 'To find out, researchers conducted' — 목적의 to부정사 정상
❌ ④ shaping: 'in shaping those results' — 전치사 in 뒤 동명사 정상
det.tip: 시제 일치: 주절이 과거(told)이면 종속절도 과거완료(had been made)

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers ①<u>would pay</u> more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product ②<u>were</u> relatively ③<u>homogeneously</u>. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior ④<u>rewarded</u> the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① would pay=지불하겠지(가정법 정상), ② were=이라면(가정법 과거 정상), ③ homogeneous→homogeneously 오류(be동사 보어 자리에 형용사 필요), ④ rewarded=보상했다(과거동사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① would pay: 'consumers would pay more' — 가정법 과거 주절 would+동사원형 정상
❌ ② were: 'if the product were relatively homogeneous' — 가정법 과거 if절에 were 사용 정상
✅ ③ homogeneously: be동사(were)의 보어 자리는 형용사(homogeneous)여야 함. homogeneously(부사)는 보어 자리 불가 ← 정답
❌ ④ rewarded: 'People rewarded the ethical companies' — 과거동사 정상
det.tip: be동사의 보어 자리에는 형용사. homogeneous(형용사) ← 보어 / homogeneously(부사) ← 동사 수식

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than ①<u>unethical</u> companies' product if the product were relatively ②<u>homogeneous</u>. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using ③<u>low</u> ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight ④<u>premium</u> for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① unethical=비윤리적인(대비 맥락 적절), ② homogeneous=동질적인(비교 조건 맥락 적절), ③ high→low 오류(윤리 기준이 '높은' 집단이어야 실험 설계상 맞음), ④ premium=추가 가격(윤리 제품 프리미엄 맥락 적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① unethical: 'unethical companies' products' — 비윤리 기업과 대비 구조에서 적절
❌ ② homogeneous: 'if the product were relatively homogeneous' — 동일 제품 비교 조건으로 적절
✅ ③ low: 'told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards' — 높은 윤리 기준으로 만들었다고 told한 집단이 핵심. low로 바꾸면 윤리 기준 낮음→프리미엄 지불 구조 모순 ← 정답
❌ ④ premium: 'willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods' — 윤리 제품에 추가 가격 지불로 적절
det.tip: 실험 설계: one group = 높은 윤리 기준(high), another group = 낮은 윤리 기준(low). high를 low로 바꾸면 실험 조건 파괴

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a ③<u>slight</u> premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a ④<u>small</u> discount. What's more, consumer ①<u>attitudes</u> played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and ②<u>punished</u> the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① slight=약간의(소폭 프리미엄 맥락 적절), ② steep→small 오류(큰 할인이어야 맥락 맞음), ③ attitudes=태도(소비자 태도 맥락 적절), ④ punished=응징했다(비윤리 기업 응징 맥락 적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① slight: 'willing to pay a slight premium' — 약간의 프리미엄으로 적절
✅ ④ small: 'would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount' — steep(가파른, 큰) 할인이 원문. small(작은) 할인으로 바꾸면 'went much further in the other direction'과 모순 ← 정답
❌ ③ attitudes: 'consumer attitudes played a big part' — 소비자 태도가 결과 형성에 큰 역할로 적절
❌ ② punished: 'punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts' — 더 큰 할인으로 비윤리 기업에 응징으로 적절
det.tip: went much further = 비윤리 방향 반응이 훨씬 강했음 → steep(큰) 할인. small(작은)은 반대

questions.stem: 연구자들은 소비자들에게 동일한 제품을 보여주면서 그 제품의 생산 방식에 대한 서로 다른 정보를 제공하였다.

det.korean: 연구 방법: 동일 제품 + 생산 윤리 기준에 대한 다른 정보 제공 여부
det.analysis:
✅ T: 'They showed consumers the same products — coffee and t-shirts — but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used' — 동일 제품에 다른 정보 제공이 맞음 ← 정답
❌ F: 본문에 명확히 같은 제품(same products)에 서로 다른 정보 제공했다고 기술
det.tip: the same products + told one group [high] / another group [low] = 동일 제품 + 상이한 정보

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 실험에서 소비자들은 비윤리적으로 만든 제품을 구매하려면 상당한 할인이 필요했으나, 윤리 제품에는 약간의 추가 가격만 지불하려 했다.

det.korean: 비윤리 제품 큰 할인 요구 + 윤리 제품 약간 프리미엄 대비 구조 일치 여부
det.analysis:
✅ T: 'consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount' — 약간 프리미엄(윤리) vs 큰 할인(비윤리) 대비 구조가 정확히 일치 ← 정답
❌ F: 본문 내용과 완전히 일치하므로 F는 틀림
det.tip: slight premium(윤리) ↔ steep discount(비윤리) — 두 방향 비대칭 반응

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 이 실험에서 소비자들은 윤리적 제품에 지불하려 한 추가 가격과 비윤리적 제품에 요구한 할인 폭이 거의 비슷했다.

det.korean: 윤리 제품 프리미엄 폭 vs 비윤리 제품 할인 폭 비교 — 비슷한지 여부
det.analysis:
❌ T: 두 방향 반응 폭이 비슷하지 않음
✅ F: 'they went much further in the other direction' — 비윤리 방향(큰 할인)으로의 반응이 윤리 방향(약간 프리미엄)보다 훨씬 컸음. 비슷하다는 진술은 거짓 ← 정답
det.tip: slight premium(약간 프리미엄) vs steep discount(큰 할인) — 비대칭 반응. much further = 훨씬 더 나아감

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비윤리 제품 구매 조건 — steep ___ (빈칸에 들어갈 단어)
det.analysis:
❌ ① premium: 프리미엄은 윤리 제품 구매 시 추가 지불 개념. 비윤리 제품에 steep premium은 맥락 반대
❌ ② reward: 보상은 윤리 기업에 주는 것. steep reward는 비윤리 제품 구매 조건과 맞지 않음
✅ ③ discount: 'would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount' — 비윤리 제품을 큰 할인에서만 구매하는 맥락에 정확히 부합 ← 정답
❌ ④ experiment: 실험은 연구 방법이지 가격 조건이 아님
det.tip: went much further in the other direction(반대 방향으로 훨씬 더) → steep discount(큰 할인)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 실험 결과를 형성한 주요 요인 — 빈칸 구절
det.analysis:
❌ ① a control group got no information: 대조군이 정보를 받지 않은 것은 사실이지만, 이것이 What's more 이후의 추가 사실 설명에 해당하지 않음. 빈칸 뒤의 'in shaping those results'와 구조 불일치
❌ ② researchers conducted a series of experiments: 연구자들이 실험을 실시한 것은 앞에서 이미 언급. 결과를 형성한 요인이 아님
❌ ③ the product itself shaped the results: 제품 자체가 아닌 소비자 태도가 결과 요인. 같은 제품을 사용했음
✅ ④ consumer attitudes played a big part: 'What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results' — 소비자 태도가 결과 형성에 큰 역할이라는 문맥과 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: What's more = 더욱이(추가 핵심 정보). consumer attitudes → shaping results가 결론 문장

det.korean: 본문 내용 일치 여부 — 정보 없는 집단 행동 확인
det.analysis:

✅ ④ 불일치: 'A control group got no information' — 아무 정보도 받지 못한 집단(통제군)은 윤리 기준 정보를 전혀 받지 않음. ④는 반대 내용 ← 정답

ch: 연구자들은 커피와 티셔츠를 실험 도구로 활용했다.

소비자들은 비윤리적 제품을 구매할 때 상당한 가격 인하를 요구했다.
아무 정보도 제공받지 못한 집단은 제품이 윤리적으로 만들어졌다는 말을 들었다.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문과 일치하는 내용 찾기
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일치: 'they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount' — 윤리 방향(약간 프리미엄)보다 비윤리 방향(큰 할인)으로 훨씬 더 강하게 반응 ← 정답
❌ ② 불일치: 품질 비교는 본문에 없음. 같은 제품 사용
❌ ③ 불일치: 'People with high standards for corporate behavior' — 높은 기준 소비자가 더 큰 프리미엄 지불. 낮은 기준이 아님
❌ ④ 불일치: 'conducted a series of experiments' — 여러 번 실험
det.tip: went much further = 비윤리 방향(할인)으로의 반응이 윤리 방향(프리미엄)보다 훨씬 강했음

ch: 소비자들은 비윤리 제품에 윤리 제품보다 훨씬 강한 가격 반응을 보였다.
윤리적으로 생산된 제품은 비윤리 제품보다 품질이 우수하다고 실험에서 밝혀졌다.
기업 행동 기준이 낮은 소비자가 윤리 기업에 더 큰 프리미엄을 지불했다.
연구자들은 단 한 번의 실험으로 소비자의 가격 지불 의향을 확인했다.

What's more, consumer attitudes ②<u>played</u> a big part in shaping those results. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① another=또 다른(단수 명사 앞 정상), ② slight=약간의(형용사 정상), ③ further→farther 오류(추상적 정도 의미에는 further 사용), ④ played=맡았다(과거동사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ④ another: 'told one group... and another group' — one A and another B 구문으로 정상
❌ ② slight: 'a slight premium' — 관사+형용사+명사 구조 정상
✅ ① farther: 'they went much further in the other direction' — further는 추상적 정도·수준의 비교에 사용. farther는 물리적 거리 비교에 사용. 여기서는 반응의 정도(추상)이므로 further가 맞음. farther로 바꾸면 어법상 부적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ played: 'consumer attitudes played a big part' — 과거 동사 정상
det.tip: further(추상적 정도/수준 비교) vs farther(물리적 거리 비교). 'went much further'는 추상적 반응 강도 표현 → further가 맞음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
